title: Onset kinetics on a resolved neighbour cell: where a whole-cell threshold and a local one disagree
description:
A pre-registered pilot study. A published two-cell study (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23253738) solved the neighbour of a failing LG M50 cell twice with identical inputs, as a single temperature (lumped) and as a resolved three-dimensional field, and compared both with fixed onset temperatures. This study replaces the fixed temperatures with the B-CRNN decomposition kinetics of Koenig, Zhao and Deng (Chemical Engineering Journal 507 (2025) 160402), integrated along the archived histories of the resolved hottest node, the resolved mean and the lumped node: the posterior-mean model passively (Stage 1, 49 cases) and as a heat source in both models (Stage 2, reactive and one-way, five cases); 200 joint draws of the kinetic posterior and 30 Latin hypercube draws of the roll's published thermal properties (Stage 3); and each of the posterior's three submodels varied alone over the same draws, the other two at their posterior mean (Stage 4, version 1.1.0). Stage 5 (version 1.2.0) sets both neighbours, with the cans in contact and joined by welded tabs, against the measured two-cell propagation tests of Fransson et al. (Journal of Power Sources 617 (2024) 234916, CC BY 4.0). Stage 6 (also version 1.2.0) applies the paper's 150 C criterion to the Stage 5 runs and gives the trigger the durations and peaks the tests measured. Stage 7 (version 1.3.0) scores the model test by test: each test gets its own trigger, seven candidate ignition conditions are read from the runs with a fresh and an aged SEI, and the internal short is run as an event, the neighbour's stored electrical energy released when its separator melts. Stage 8 (version 1.4.0) asks, test by test, what fraction of the trigger's ejected energy, delivered to the neighbour, the model would need to reproduce each outcome. Through Stage 7, conduction and radiation only between the cells: venting, ejecta and flame are excluded; Stage 8 adds a part of the ejected energy, delivered as a flux into the neighbour's can, its size found rather than set. Stages 1 to 4 concern onset in a neighbour; Stages 5 to 8 ask whether, and when, the neighbour propagates. Each stage's predictions were committed and pushed before its kinetics ran on an archived history (commits b09ef1d and 2657aee), Stage 4's before any grouped run (a975f20), Stage 5's before any Stage 5 run (b4883ba), Stage 6's before any Stage 6 computation (c9586a8), Stage 7's before any Stage 7 run (714b1fd), and Stage 8's before any Stage 8 run (b8dafb4).

Results

  • With copper busbars (500 mW/K in all) and the largest Battery Failure Databank energy (33.2 kJ), the resolved hottest node starts to self-heat at 0.15 K/min 23.4 s and 26.4 s before the lumped node (4.2 against 27.6 s for a 10 s release, 11.5 against 37.9 s for 30 s). Under the posterior-mean kinetics every start is a fresh SEI decomposing at 108.4 C.
  • The smallest busbar conductance at which only the local chemistry starts is 100 mW/K under the posterior-mean kinetics (21.5 kJ); across the kinetic posterior it spreads over six of the seven conductances from 5 to 500 mW/K.
  • With the reaction heat fed back, the hottest node enters the internal-short band (255.7 C) at the same moment as without it, so the entry is set by conduction. The lumped cell never enters the band, yet releases 6.0 and 7.1 times the resolved cell's reaction heat.
  • Over 200 draws of the kinetic posterior the lumped node never starts before the hottest node, in any of the 42 two-strip cases. At 33.2 kJ, 30 s and 500 mW/K the lead runs from 15.4 to 58.9 s (2.5 to 97.5 %, median 26.3 s); 36.5 % of the draws start below 100 C, by SEI decomposition.
  • At that case, over the published spread of the roll's conductivity and heat capacity (contact, busbar and emissivity held fixed), the hottest node's onset varies 0.027 times as much as over the kinetic posterior and the lumped node's 0.11 times (standard deviations): the kinetics set both onsets.
  • The anode-electrolyte submodel, which holds the SEI decomposition, carries essentially all of the lead's variance. Varied alone it gives 0.997 of the lead's variance over the joint draws at 33.2 kJ, 30 s and 500 mW/K (paired bootstrap 0.92 to 1.09), and 0.89 to 1.09 of every output's at 500 and 100 mW/K; the NCM811 cathode gives 0.000 and the separator 0.001 to 0.002. Exploratory analysis shows that the separator's melting still decides the mode of 13 marginal draws. With it at its posterior mean no draw starts below 100 C, against 37.5 % with it varied.
  • Restricting the anode-electrolyte submodel to the half of its particles closest to the posterior mean (a parameter-space proxy for a tighter posterior) narrows the lead's 2.5 to 97.5 % interval only from 43.5 to 37.1 s (14.6 %; 18.1 % when the half is chosen on the SEI decomposition's own parameters). Exploratory analysis, written after the results, traces this to the lead's two modes (hottest-node starts by 122.4 C, or at 184.9 C and above), both of which a tighter posterior keeps.
  • Stage 5: the tests propagated in 9 of 16, at 147 to 342 s. With a steel-on-steel line contact of 200, 2,000 and 3,700 W/(m2 K) (a textbook table's range, so every result is conditional on it), welded tabs bracketed by the two-cell study's nickel strip, and 33.2 kJ at an assumed 100 % state of charge, neither neighbour reaches 255.7 C within 900 s in any of 5,248 runs, which cover all 200 kinetic draws. In the central case (central contact and tabs) the resolved hot spot, on the line of contact, peaks at 191.5 to 192.3 C and the lumped neighbour at 159.4 to 162.1 C; the highest peaks of any run are 226.7 C (resolved) and 180.6 C (lumped). The model was expected to propagate later than the tests, if at all, because it lacks their venting, ejecta and flame; it does not propagate at all within 900 s.
  • Stage 6: under the paper's criterion, a neighbour of at least 150 C, only the lumped neighbour at the central contact crosses inside the measured 147 to 342 s, in 11 of 12 Stage 5 grid runs; the resolved hot spot crosses at 6.8 to 21.6 s, and the face away from the trigger, where the thermocouple would sit, never reaches 150 C. With the release durations of the paper's supplementary Figure 10 (17.5 to 25.2 s, conditional on an assumed start at 25 C), Stage 5's 33.2 kJ puts the trigger at 526 to 537 C in the central case, inside the sixteen measured trigger maxima (164 to 832 C), while the Databank's total with the ejecta, 107.0 kJ, puts it at 1,424 to 1,494 C. The matched trigger ignites neither neighbour in any of 442 runs, the 200 kinetic draws among them. At 107.0 kJ the hot spot reaches 255.7 C in every run at 8.2 to 17.0 s and the lumped neighbour 31.9 to 167.9 s later; with a trigger at the tests' median peak (704.5 C, 45.15 kJ, exploratory) only the high contact ignites, the hot spot at 16.7 s and the lumped neighbour at 198 to 236 s. Where the hot spot ignites it does so before any test propagated, while the lumped neighbour reaches 255.7 C inside the measured window in 13 of the 50 runs in which it does: the question moves to the ignition condition (an aged SEI, the internal short as an event), set up for a next stage.
  • Stage 7: with one trigger per test (8.98 to 54.30 kJ, which put cell 1 at each test's measured maximum, 164 to 832 C, at the central case with the median release), seven ignition conditions read from 96 runs (the sixteen tests at three contacts, with a fresh and an aged SEI) are scored against the sixteen outcomes, the central contact registered. There the hot spot at 255.7 C predicts propagation for 8 tests (6 hits, 2 false alarms; 11 of 16 right), every hit 129.6 to 322.7 s before the measured time; the lumped neighbour at 255.7 C predicts 2, both hits; the lumped neighbour at the paper's 150 C, and the separator's melting (138.5 C) at the hot spot or in the lumped neighbour, each predict the same 14 tests (8 hits, 6 false alarms; 9 of 16). At the central contact an aged SEI (initial amount 0) changes no hot-spot verdict and raises, not lowers, the hot spot's first self-heating, from 108.4 C to 181.5 to 202.1 C, and the other two releases and the separator's spread over the posterior change no verdict. Released at the melt, at the central contact, the cell's stored electrical energy (65.52 kJ over 21.39 s, a modelling choice) takes the hot spot to 1,504.5 to 1,584.3 C, about twice the hottest propagating neighbour measured (763 C): 0 of 28 runs inside the measured 381 to 763 C, and 0 of 28 at the specification's minimum, 63.36 kJ. Nothing in Part C is a source to a further cell. No criterion reproduces the outcomes test by test; the measured outcomes do not follow the trigger's maximum, so no threshold on it gets more than 12 of the 16 right (exploratory).
  • Stage 8: the inverse question, test by test. Each trigger's ejected energy (its body energy times the median ejected-to-body ratio of the Databank's ten M50 nail tests, 3.105, bracketed by their smallest and largest, 2.218 and 4.156: 27.9 to 168.6 kJ) is delivered in part to the neighbour, as a uniform flux through the half of its can facing the trigger, over 21.39 s from the start of the release, and a search finds for each test f*, the smallest fraction at which the model meets a criterion (a propagated test's outcome is reproduced at f* and above, a non-propagated test's below it). For the hot spot at 255.7 C, f* is 0 in eight tests (Stage 7's runs) and at most 0.1625 in every test (M50_PT_Exp1, the smallest trigger); for the lumped neighbour, at most 0.05 in thirteen tests and at most 0.4625 in all. The two groups overlap: the nine propagated tests need f* of 0 to 0.0875 for the hot spot (0 to 0.2375 for the lumped neighbour), while the seven that did not propagate reach it in the model at 0 to 0.1625 (0 to 0.4625). No single fraction reproduces the sixteen outcomes; if a delivered fraction set them, it would have had to vary from test to test, a quantity the tests did not control, and propagation at a given trigger would be a probability. At fractions of 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 common to all tests, the hot spot and the lumped neighbour at 255.7 C and at 150 C each predict 14 to 16 tests and get 9 or 10 of the 16 right; every clock crosses by 88.3 s after the release, and every hit comes 125.6 to 339.3 s before the measured time. Not registered: M50_PT_Exp1's f* for the hot spot, 0.15 to 0.1625, becomes 0.1 to 0.1125 over a 10 s delivery, 0.275 to 0.2875 over 60 s and 0.0375 to 0.05 at the quarter of the facing half nearest the cap, and the ratio's bracket scales every f* by 0.75 to 1.40; in the parallel tests, Joule heat of a fifth of the cell's stored 65.52 kJ alone takes every hot spot to 255.7 C. With the gas layer of Hoelle, Zimmermann and Hinrichsen (2023) between the roll and the can (their Eq. 28 and 29 and Tables V and VI), at f = 0.2 in the three tests nearest the median trigger, the hot spot does not reach 255.7 C within 900 s (it peaks at 192.4 to 196.5 C), where without the layer it does at 3.5 to 3.7 s: the layer keeps the delivered heat in the can, which reaches 1,886 to 1,924 C in the model (no melting or venting), so that the hot spot's f* there lies above 0.2; the lumped neighbour, one node, is unchanged by construction. Exploratory, written after the results: neither a fraction drawn for each test from one log-normal distribution nor a logistic in the trigger energy fits the outcomes significantly better than one probability for every test (likelihood ratios 3.16 and 0.97, p = 0.075 and 0.32). f* is a model quantity, not a measurement of what reached the neighbour.
  • Scorecards. Stages 1 and 2: P1 to P4 held; P5(a) held, against the registered expectation; P5(b) failed; P5(c) held. Stage 3: P1, P2 and P5 held; P3, P4 and P6 failed. Stage 4: P1, P2, P3 and P5 held; P4 failed. Stage 5: P2 held, because the lumped neighbour never propagates; P1 and P6 failed; P3, P4, P5 and P7 were not met, and so failed, because no run propagated. Stage 6: P7 held (the lumped neighbour never reaches 255.7 C before the hot spot); P1 to P6 failed, P1, P2, P3, P5 and P6 foreseeably, as its predictions recorded from Stage 5's results before any Stage 6 computation. Stage 7: P1, P4 and P6 held; P2, P3, P5, P7 and P8 failed, each as its predictions expected. Stage 8: P1, P2, P5, P6 and P8 held (P6 with two tests both at 0 read as equal, not as an inversion); P3, P4 and P7 failed, each as its predictions expected.

Checks. The source's DSC curves are reproduced. An emulation of its ARC test gives T_in = 179.3 C with the posterior-mean kinetics, inside its two-sigma band (169.0 to 198.0 C), but T_on = 199.8 C at its stated 1 C/min trigger, below its band (255.7 to 302.1 C). Over the 200 kinetic draws the same emulation failed the brief's acceptance (the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of the main-cluster T_in at 146.3 and 191.4 C); after the failure was reported the author amended the check (the paper's own mean plus and minus two standard deviations, measured from the emulation's own T_in), under which it passes; both verdicts are recorded. Halving tolerances, steps and grids moves the onsets by at most 7e-5 of themselves; energy accounts close to 1e-11 of the heat taken in at the published conductivities; with a 1e4 W/mK roll the resolved and lumped models agree within 0.8 K. Before the Stage 4 predictions, the grouped models were shown to separate exactly by submodel, and the posterior-mean model and five joint draws run through the Stage 4 path reproduce Stages 1 and 3 exactly. Before the Stage 5 predictions, every contact and tab path matched the lumped formula to 2e-16 and an analytic steady case to 5e-5 of the rise, and the Stage 5 code in the two-cell configuration reproduced Stages 1 and 2; in Stage 5, halving the mesh spacing changes the central case's peak rise by 0.27 and 0.31 % and halving the steps by under 0.005 %, the energy accounts close to within 8.5e-12 of the heat taken in, the 48 runs made on both machines agree to 1.6e-10 J and 2.9e-11 K, and an independent read of every registered number and verdict reproduced them all, and the nine discrepancies it found in the draft texts were corrected. In Stage 6, the 150 C crossings of three runs recomputed by hand agree exactly, the trigger's energies, durations and peaks re-derived by separate code agree within 4.6e-13 K, halving the mesh spacing or the steps changes the central matched case's peak rise by at most 0.32 %, the energy accounts close to within 8.5e-12 of the heat taken in, and an independent read of every registered Stage 6 number and verdict reproduced them all; the discrepancies it found in the draft texts were corrected. In Stage 7, the sixteen energies re-derived from the peak-to-energy table agree within 0.64 J, the crossings of three runs recomputed by hand agree exactly, halving the mesh spacing or the steps changes the post-event peak rise of one event run by at most 0.15 %, the energy accounts close to within 4.34e-12 of the heat taken in with the event's energy in them, every event delivers its energy exactly, and an independent read of every registered Stage 7 number and verdict reproduced them all; the errata it found in two design entries are recorded, and the two checks that did less than their decisions say and the wording points it found were corrected. In Stage 8, the ratios and the ejected energies re-derived by separate code agree to 5.3e-15, the six searches of C1 and C2 for three tests, replayed from the records by separate code, give the same brackets, halving the mesh spacing or the steps changes one run's hot-spot peak rise by at most 0.52 %, the energy accounts close to within 1.97e-11 of the heat taken in with every delivered and Joule energy exact, and an independent read of every registered Stage 8 number and verdict reproduced them all; the errata it found in three design entries (D79 (1), D80 and D86 (2)) and in the predictions' background are recorded, and the labels, the thresholds file, V2's replay and the wording points it found were corrected, with no registered number or verdict changed.

Limits. Kinetics from other cells (NCM811 and graphite DSC data, the source cell's reactant fractions) with a fresh SEI; Stage 3 treats the posterior's three submodels as independent, and its thermal ranges are literature spreads (O'Regan et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2021), not measured uncertainties of this cell; Stage 4 holds two submodels at their posterior mean, and its central half is a parameter-space proxy for a tighter posterior, not a simulated measurement; Stage 1 ignores the reaction heat and Stage 2 is one-way; conduction and radiation only; Stages 1 to 4 use one geometry without the cap and tabs; Stage 5's contact conductance is a textbook range for steel on steel, its tabs a bracket from the two-cell study, its state of charge assumed, and it has no venting, ejecta or flame; Stage 6's release durations come from two tests with an assumed start temperature, and its propagation level, 255.7 C at the hottest node, from a fresh-SEI posterior trained on other cells; Stage 7's triggers are matched at the central contact only, its aged SEI is the limiting case of none left, and its event, all the stored electrical energy released at the melt, is a modelling choice with no path for venting or ejecta; Stage 8's threshold fraction is a model quantity, the fraction a conduction-and-delivery model needs, not a measurement of what reached the neighbour, its delivery one geometry and duration among many (the cap end and the 10 and 60 s durations are brackets, none claimed as the tests'), its electrical path a bracket on Joule heat with the state of charge it removes outside the kinetics, and its gas layer one taken from another cell stack's model.
